title: The Impact of Shift Work on the Performance of Remote Train Operators in a Control Center Scenario
summary: Rail transportation of the future will be characterized by a high degree of automation, and the operation of trains without a train operator in the cab is a likely scenario. As a result, the role of the traditional locomotive engineer will evolve into that of a remote operator who monitors the automated trains from a rail control center and takes control of individual trains only in the event of malfunctions or unforeseen incidents. In addition to the changed job requirements, working in shifts continues to pose a challenge. This is because the fatigue associated with shift work—for example, during an early shift following typically reduced sleep—can impair operators’ performance and thus jeopardize rail safety. As part of the CaRe4Rail study, the impact of shift work on the performance of remote operators will be examined in a simulated rail control center environment. The resolution of operational disruptions in the simulation—under varying workloads during an early shift—will be compared to performance during a day shift. In addition, the workload will be assessed through additional performance tests, questionnaires, and physiological parameters (eye movement, heart rate).
conditions: The Effects of Sleep Deprivation on Performance

interventions.name:
Early shift (shortened sleep)
During the shift, participants complete four scenarios with varying workloads, which are presented in a balanced order.

Day shift (normal sleep)
During the shift, participants complete four scenarios with varying workloads, presented in a balanced order.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Submission of the signed data protection consent form, the
participant agreement, the privacy policy for the study, and the
participant consent form
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language
Exclusion criteria:
- Participation in the NGT-BIT Study 2021
- Insufficient knowledge of German
- Any medication that may affect the test parameters
- Drug addiction, smoking
- Vision or hearing problems that interfere with
eye movement measurement or auditory performance tests
- Acute or chronic medical conditions that may affect performance
during the test
- BMI > 35
- Atypical sleep habits:
a) On weekdays: Going to bed before 9:00 PM or after midnight, waking up before
5:00 AM or after 8:30 AM
b) Regular sleep duration < 7 and > 9 hours (nighttime sleep) on weekdays
- Suspected sleep apnea syndrome
